cards.text: David has died, and Solomon now sits on his father's throne (1 Kings 2:10-12). Adonijah, Solomon's brother who once tried to make himself king (1 Kings 1:5), goes to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She has one question for him right away.

cards.question: Adonijah has come to see Bathsheba. What does she ask him?

answers.text: Does the king know you are here
Why have you come to me

cards.text: Adonijah says yes, in peace, and then he tells her the kingship was his and all Israel expected him to reign. That's a BOLD way to open a visit with the new king's MOTHER.

cards.question: Adonijah admits the kingship has turned to his brother Solomon. He says it came to Solomon from ___.

cards.text: Then he says he has just one request, and he wants Bathsheba to bring it to King Solomon, because Solomon will not turn her down. Just one, he says. I said that about chocolate chips once, friend, and now I own FORTY bags.

cards.question: What does Adonijah want Bathsheba to ask King Solomon to give him?

answers.text: Abishag the Shunammite as his wife
Command over the king's whole army
A city of his own to rule over

cards.text: Abishag is the young woman who cared for King David in his old age (1 Kings 1:1-4). Bathsheba says, “Very well,” and promises to speak to the king for Adonijah.

cards.question: When Bathsheba comes in to see him, King Solomon stands up to greet her and bows to her.
Then King Solomon has something brought in for his mother. What is it?

answers.text: A throne at his right hand

cards.text: Bathsheba tells her son she has just one small request, and adds, “Do not deny me.” She said SMALL, friend, so hold onto your apron.

cards.question: Before he even hears what it is, King Solomon tells his mother he will not deny her request.

cards.text: So Bathsheba asks for Abishag the Shunammite to be given to Adonijah as his wife. Solomon answers his mother with a question of his own: why ask for Abishag for Adonijah?

cards.question: Solomon points out that Adonijah is his older brother. He tells his mother she might as well request the ___ for him.
Solomon says that request for Adonijah would also be a request for two other men. Who are they?

cards.text: Those two backed Adonijah when he tried to become king: Abiathar the priest, and Joab, the commander of David's army (1 Kings 1:7; 2 Samuel 8:16).
Then King Solomon swears by the LORD, the One who set him on the throne of his father David. That “just one request” is not looking so little anymore.

cards.question: Solomon swears that Adonijah will be sent away from Jerusalem.
King Solomon gives the orders to ___ son of Jehoiada.

cards.text: Benaiah strikes Adonijah down, and he dies. Heavy day in Jerusalem, friend, and Solomon isn't done yet.
Next, King Solomon speaks to Abiathar the priest. He says Abiathar deserves to die, but he will not put him to death at this time.

cards.question: Instead, Solomon tells Abiathar to go back to his ___ in Anathoth.
Solomon gives a reason for sparing Abiathar's life. What is it?

answers.text: He carried the ark before David
He begged the king for mercy
Zadok the priest spoke for him

cards.text: So Solomon banishes Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD. And with that, a word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh is fulfilled.

cards.question: The word the LORD spoke at Shiloh was against someone's house. Whose?

cards.text: The news reaches Joab, who had conspired with Adonijah but not with Absalom. And Joab RUNS, faster than me when the smoke alarm goes off over a batch.

cards.question: Joab has heard the news and he's on the run. Where does he go?

answers.text: To the tent of the LORD

cards.question: Once Joab gets there, he takes hold of the horns of the altar.

cards.text: Solomon hears where Joab is and sends Benaiah: “Go, strike him down!” Benaiah enters the tent of the LORD and tells Joab, “The king says, ‘Come out!’”

cards.question: Benaiah tells Joab to come out. What does Joab say back?

answers.text: Let me speak to the king

cards.text: Benaiah goes back and reports Joab's answer to the king. Solomon's reply: “Do just as he says.”

cards.question: Solomon says Joab struck down two men without his father David knowing. Who were they?
Solomon calls those two men more righteous and better than Joab.

cards.text: Solomon says their blood will come back on Joab and his descendants, but for David, his descendants, his house, and his throne, “there shall be peace from the LORD forever.” Then Benaiah goes up, strikes Joab down, and kills him.

cards.question: Joab is buried at his own home in the ___.

cards.text: Now two jobs are open: Joab's place over the army, and Abiathar's place as priest. Solomon fills them both.

cards.question: Solomon puts Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab's place.
In Abiathar's place, Solomon appoints ___ the priest.

cards.text: Then King Solomon summons Shimei, the man who called down bitter curses against David (1 Kings 2:8). Solomon tells him to build a house for himself in Jerusalem and live there.

cards.question: Solomon tells Shimei he can still come and go from Jerusalem as he pleases.

cards.text: Solomon names the line Shimei must not cross: the Kidron Valley. It's like the DO NOT TOUCH sign on my cooling rack, except this one is very, VERY serious.

cards.question: What does Solomon say will happen on the day Shimei crosses the Kidron Valley?

answers.text: He will be put in chains

cards.question: How does Shimei answer the king's terms?

cards.text: And Shimei lives in Jerusalem for a long time. So far, so good.

cards.question: After ___ years, two of Shimei's slaves run away.
Shimei's slaves run away to Achish, king of ___.

cards.text: Somebody tells Shimei, “Look, your slaves are in Gath.” So he saddles his donkey and heads out, and friend, I am YELLING at the page right now.

cards.question: Shimei finds his slaves in Gath and brings them back.

cards.text: Solomon is told Shimei went to Gath and came back, so he summons him. Then he reads Shimei his own words, “The sentence is fair; I will comply,” and that's worse than a boss reading your old email out loud in a meeting.

cards.question: Solomon asks why Shimei has not kept the king's command, and one more thing. What is it?

cards.text: Solomon tells Shimei he knows in his heart all the evil he did to David. So the LORD will bring his evil back upon his head.

cards.question: Then Solomon speaks about himself and his father's throne. What does he say about David's throne?

answers.text: It will be shared with his brothers
It will be shaken for a while

cards.text: Then the king commands Benaiah, who goes out and strikes Shimei down, and he dies. Heavy chapter, friend.

cards.question: By the end of all this, the kingdom is firmly established in Solomon's hand.

findings.problem: The chocolate chip joke doesn't match the action. Adonijah makes one request that is bigger than it sounds. 'Just one bag turned into forty bags' is about buying more and more, not about one request that hides something big. It also hints that Adonijah has more requests coming, which the text never says.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This card cites 1 Kings 2:22 but tells nothing from the passage. It only gives background from 1 Kings 1:7 and 2 Samuel 8:16, so it doesn't move the baker forward. The introduction of Abiathar and Joab could ride on a card that also carries a moment of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: No card ever tells what Solomon actually swears in 1 Kings 2:23-24: that Adonijah made this request at the expense of his life and will be put to death that very day. Card 16 holds the oath back, and card 17 only rules out a false version of it. The baker learns what the oath was not, never what it was, so the key turn of the stop is missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Benaiah son of Jehoiada appears here for the first time, and no card ever says who he is. He shows up again throughout stops 2 and 3.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says Solomon 'gives the orders' without saying what the orders are about. The oath was never told (see card 17), so the question leaves the baker with no context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: Absalom is named for the first time without saying who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Joab flees for his life. A baker runs to the oven when the smoke alarm goes off, toward the problem to save the batch. Those aren't the same action, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Abner and Amasa appear for the first time and are never introduced. Yet the text itself says who they are in 1 Kings 2:32: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Wilderness, valley or mountains is a pure guess, because nothing before this card hints at where Joab is buried. It's also a minor detail that doesn't move the passage. The walkthrough already has many discovery questions (for example stop 1 card 18, stop 2 cards 2, 5, 12 and 18, and stop 3 cards 7 and 8), so this one tips the balance away from informed guesses.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Three, seven or ten years can only be guessed. Card 6 says only 'a long time,' which fits all three answers. Together with the many other discovery questions in this walkthrough, most choice cards are no longer informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
